source.text: שִׁמְע֣וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear the word which has spoken Yahweh to you, house of Israel.

en.L: Hear the word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken to you, house of Israel.
en.B: Hear the word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken to you, house of Israel.
en.R: People of Israel, listen to the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has for you.

decisions.choice: house of Israel: the whole covenant people, here those living in Judah
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom had fallen to Assyria long before (2 Kings 17:6). Jeremiah still calls the people of Judah and Jerusalem by the old name of the whole nation descended from Jacob (2:4; 9:25), the people bound to God by his covenant.

decisions.choice: to you: addressed to you
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "to" or "concerning"; here it introduces the people the message is spoken to, as the call "hear" shows.

decisions.choice: People of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "people of Israel" for "house of Israel", since "house" here means a family line, not a building, and puts the call to listen first, as a plain call to attention.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַגּוֹיִם֙ אַל־תִּלְמָ֔דוּ וּמֵאֹת֥וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם אַל־תֵּחָ֑תּוּ כִּֽי־יֵחַ֥תּוּ הַגּוֹיִ֖ם מֵהֵֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: to [the] way of the nations do not learn, and at [the] signs of the heavens do not be dismayed, for are dismayed the nations at them.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Do not learn the way of the nations, \q and do not be dismayed at the signs of the heavens, \q for the nations are dismayed at them.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Do not take up the ways of the nations, \q and do not be terrified by signs in the sky, \q though the nations are terrified by them.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Do not copy the way the other nations live. \q Do not be afraid of strange signs in the sky. \q Let the other nations be afraid of them.

decisions.choice: the way of the nations: their customs, above all in worship
decisions.reason: "Way" is a manner of life. The next verse names it as the "customs of the peoples", and the whole poem (verses 3-5, 8-9, 14-15) shows that their worship of idols is meant. Israel is not to learn it (Leviticus 18:3; Deuteronomy 18:9).

decisions.choice: the signs of the heavens: eclipses, comets and other sights in the sky read as omens
decisions.reason: The peoples of Mesopotamia kept long records of what they saw in the sky and read it as warnings about kings and nations. Israel was told not to worship the sun, moon and stars or treat them as powers (Deuteronomy 4:19), since God made them (Genesis 1:14-18).

decisions.choice: be dismayed: be shattered with fear
decisions.reason: The verb means to be broken down by terror (1:17; Isaiah 30:31). The same verb is used of Israel and of the nations, to set the two side by side.

decisions.choice: for: the nations' fear is theirs, not Israel's
decisions.reason: The joining word gives the reason not to be afraid: these signs frighten the nations, who do not know the God who made the heavens (verses 11-12). It can also be read "though" with the same sense.

decisions.choice: though (Balanced); Let the other nations be afraid of them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "though" so that the reason reads naturally; Readable turns it into a short statement that the fear belongs to the nations and not to Israel (meaning decision m4). Readable also adds "other" and "strange" to make clear who and what is meant.

source.text: כִּֽי־חֻקּ֥וֹת הָֽעַמִּ֖ים הֶ֣בֶל ה֑וּא כִּֽי־עֵץ֙ מִיַּ֣עַר כְּרָת֔וֹ מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵ֥י־חָרָ֖שׁ בַּֽמַּעֲצָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: For [the] customs of the peoples futility [is] it; for a tree from [the] forest one cuts it, [the] work of [the] hands of a craftsman with the tool.

en.L: For the customs of the peoples [are] futility; \q for a tree from the forest someone cuts down, \q the work of the hands of a craftsman with the tool.
en.B: The customs of the peoples are empty breath: \q a tree is cut down from the forest \q and worked by a craftsman's hands with his tool.
en.R: The way these nations worship is worthless. \q Someone cuts down a tree in the forest, \q and a skilled worker shapes it with his tools.

decisions.choice: customs: the fixed rites and practices of the peoples' religion
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for God's own statutes. Here it is the set customs of other peoples (Leviticus 18:3, 30; 20:23), and the verse at once describes what they are: making an idol.

decisions.choice: futility: breath, vapor, something with no substance
decisions.reason: The word means a breath of air and so what is empty and passes away. It is a key word in this poem (verses 8 and 15, where it names the idols themselves) and recalls 2:5, where Israel "went after futility and became futile".

decisions.choice: the tool: a cutting tool, perhaps an adze or an axe
decisions.reason: The word appears only here and in Isaiah 44:12. It is an iron tool used to shape wood or metal; its exact form is not known.

decisions.choice: a tree from the forest made into a god
decisions.reason: The picture follows Isaiah's satire of idol making, where a man cuts down a tree, burns half of it and carves a god from the rest (Isaiah 44:9-20; 40:19-20). The point is the same: the god is only what human hands have made from wood.

decisions.choice: empty breath (Balanced); The way these nations worship is worthless (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture in "futility" with "empty breath" and leaves the opening "for" unsaid, since the verse begins the reason for verse 2 without needing the word. Readable says plainly which customs are meant (meaning decision m1) and uses "worthless" for the empty breath.

source.text: בְּכֶ֥סֶף וּבְזָהָ֖ב יְיַפֵּ֑הוּ בְּמַסְמְר֧וֹת וּבְמַקָּב֛וֹת יְחַזְּק֖וּם וְל֥וֹא יָפִֽיק׃

records.literal_gloss: With silver and with gold he beautifies it; with nails and with hammers they fasten them, and not it will totter.

en.L: With silver and with gold he makes it beautiful; \q with nails and with hammers they fasten them, so that it will not totter.
en.B: He decorates it with silver and gold; \q they fix it in place with hammer and nails so that it will not topple over.
en.R: He covers it with silver and gold. \q Then they use hammers and nails to fix it in place so that it will not fall over.

decisions.choice: with silver and with gold: a wooden image overlaid with precious metal
decisions.reason: Idols were often carved from wood and then covered with thin sheets of silver or gold (verse 9; Isaiah 40:19; 30:22).

decisions.choice: he ... they ... them: the craftsman, then the workers, then the idols in general
decisions.reason: The verse moves from one craftsman to the people who help him, and from one idol to idols in general. The change shows a whole trade at work, not one person.

decisions.choice: fastened with nails so that it will not totter
decisions.reason: Isaiah mocks the same thing: an idol must be fastened with nails so that it does not topple (Isaiah 41:7; 40:20). A god that has to be held up cannot hold anyone else up.

decisions.choice: covers it
decisions.reason: Readable says "covers" for "makes beautiful", since the beauty is the silver and gold laid over the wood (meaning decision m1).

source.text: כְּתֹ֨מֶר מִקְשָׁ֥ה הֵ֨מָּה֙ וְלֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ נָשׂ֥וֹא יִנָּשׂ֖וּא כִּ֣י לֹ֣א יִצְעָ֑דוּ אַל־תִּֽירְא֤וּ מֵהֶם֙ כִּי־לֹ֣א יָרֵ֔עוּ וְגַם־הֵיטֵ֖יב אֵ֥ין אוֹתָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Like a scarecrow of a cucumber field they [are], and not they speak; surely they are carried, for not they walk. Do not fear them, for not they do harm, and also doing good not [is] in them.

en.L: Like a scarecrow in a cucumber field [are] they, and they do not speak; \q they must surely be carried, for they do not walk. \q Do not be afraid of them, for they cannot do harm, \q and also doing good is not in them.
en.B: Like a scarecrow in a cucumber patch, they cannot speak; \q they have to be carried, for they cannot walk. \q Do not be afraid of them: they can do no harm, \q and they have no power to do good either.
en.R: Idols are like scarecrows in a cucumber field. They cannot talk. \q People have to carry them, because they cannot walk. \q Do not be afraid of them. They cannot hurt you, \q and they cannot help you either.

decisions.choice: a scarecrow in a cucumber field
alternatives: like a palm tree of hammered work
like a post in a cucumber field
decisions.reason: The phrase is rare and its sense is not certain. The first word elsewhere means a palm tree (Judges 4:5), and the second can mean a cucumber field (Isaiah 1:8) or hammered metalwork (Exodus 25:18). Read as a scarecrow, it pictures a stiff figure set up in a field that frightens no one who knows what it is; a later Jewish writing, the Letter of Jeremiah, uses the same picture of idols. Read the other way, it is "like a palm-shaped post of hammered work", an upright pillar that cannot speak.

decisions.choice: they must surely be carried: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb ("carrying, they are carried") to stress it. Isaiah sets the gods that must be carried against the God who carries his people (Isaiah 46:1-7).

decisions.choice: do harm ... do good: do anything at all
decisions.reason: Harm and good together form a pair that covers everything; to say the idols can do neither is to say they can do nothing (Isaiah 41:23; Zephaniah 1:12).

decisions.choice: Idols ... People have to carry them ... hurt you ... help you
decisions.reason: Readable names the idols, says who carries them and puts doing harm and doing good as hurting and helping the people addressed (meaning decision m3).

source.text: מֵאֵ֥ין כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה וְגָד֥וֹל שִׁמְךָ֖ בִּגְבוּרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: There is none like you, Yahweh; great [are] you, and great [is] your name in might.

en.L: There is none like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] great, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name [is] great in might.
en.B: No one is like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are great, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is great in power.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, there is no one like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You are great, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is great and powerful.

decisions.choice: verses 6-8 and 10 as the Hebrew text has them
alternatives: omit verses 6-8 and 10, with verse 9 after the first part of verse 5
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has these verses of praise between the descriptions of idol making. The old Greek translation of Jeremiah, which is shorter than the Hebrew throughout, does not have verses 6-8 and 10, and it places verse 9 inside verse 5, so the description of the idols runs on without a break. A fragment of Jeremiah found at Qumran seems to share the shorter form. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: the speaker turns to God in praise
decisions.reason: After God's words about the idols, the prophet speaks to God directly. The change is not marked in the Hebrew. The lines of praise (verses 6-7, 10, 12-16) alternate with the lines about idols, setting the living God against the made gods.

decisions.choice: there is none: an emphatic "none at all"
decisions.reason: The negative here has an extra preposition in front of it, which strengthens it: there is no one whatever like God (also verse 7).

decisions.choice: your name: God as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person and his reputation. God's name is great in might because of what he has shown himself to be in his acts (Exodus 15:3; Psalm 8:2).

decisions.choice: LORD first
decisions.reason: Readable puts the call to God first so that the change of speaker is clear at once (meaning decision m2).

source.text: מִ֣י לֹ֤א יִֽרָאֲךָ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּ֥י לְךָ֖ יָאָ֑תָה כִּ֣י בְכָל־חַכְמֵ֧י הַגּוֹיִ֛ם וּבְכָל־מַלְכוּתָ֖ם מֵאֵ֥ין כָּמֽוֹךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Who not would fear you, king of the nations? For to you it is fitting; for among all [the] wise of the nations and in all their kingdom there is none like you.

en.L: Who would not fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, King of the nations? \q For it is fitting for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q for among all the wise of the nations and in all their kingdom there is none like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: Who would not fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, King of the nations? \q That is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} due. \q Among all the wise of the nations and in all their kingdoms there is no one like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: King of the nations, who would not fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? \q Everyone ought to fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Among all the wise people of the nations, in all their kingdoms, there is no one like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: fear you: hold you in awe and honor
decisions.reason: To fear God is to stand in awe of him and give him the honor that is his (5:22, 24; Deuteronomy 10:12). The question expects the answer "no one".

decisions.choice: King of the nations: God rules all peoples, not only Israel
decisions.reason: The idols belong to the nations, but the nations themselves belong to God (Psalm 22:29; 47:9). The words are echoed in the song of Revelation 15:3-4: "Who will not fear, Lord ... King of the nations?"

decisions.choice: it is fitting: it is your due
decisions.reason: The verb appears only here. It means that something suits or is owed to someone: fear and honor are rightly God's.

decisions.choice: their kingdom: their royal rule, all their realms
decisions.reason: The noun is singular, "their kingship" or "realm", taken together for all the kingdoms of the wise men of the nations.

decisions.choice: That is your due (Balanced); Everyone ought to fear you (Readable); kingdoms
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is fitting in plain words; Readable repeats the verb "fear" from the question so the link is clear. Both use the plural "kingdoms" for the singular collective (meaning decision m4).

source.text: וּבְאַחַ֖ת יִבְעֲר֣וּ וְיִכְסָ֑לוּ מוּסַ֥ר הֲבָלִ֖ים עֵ֥ץ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And in one they are stupid and they are foolish; [the] instruction of futilities, wood [is] it.

en.L: And all together they are stupid and foolish; \q the instruction of futilities: it [is] wood.
en.B: They are senseless and foolish, all of them alike; \q the teaching of empty idols is only a block of wood.
en.R: All of them are stupid and foolish. \q Their idols are only wood; they have nothing to teach.

decisions.choice: they: the wise men and peoples of the nations (verse 7)
decisions.reason: The verse follows on from "the wise of the nations". For all their wisdom, they are senseless together, "as one" (the meaning of the phrase translated "all together").

decisions.choice: stupid and foolish: dull as an animal, without sense
decisions.reason: The first verb comes from the word for cattle and means to be brutish, without understanding. It returns in verse 14 for idol makers and in verse 21 for Judah's own leaders.

decisions.choice: the instruction of futilities: it is wood: what idols teach is no more than the wood they are
alternatives: the discipline of worthless things is wood
an idol's teaching is a stick of wood
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and hard. It probably means that whatever guidance people seek from idols comes from a piece of wood and is worth nothing. It could also be read "the discipline of idols is wood", that is, the idol worshipper's training is worthless, or as a mocking reply: "the idols' instruction? It is a stick!"

decisions.choice: futilities: idols, called empty breaths
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for "breath" in verse 3 is a scornful name for idols (8:19; 14:22; Deuteronomy 32:21).

decisions.choice: empty idols ... only a block of wood (Balanced); Their idols are only wood; they have nothing to teach (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the idols and spell out that their teaching is as empty as the wood they are carved from (meaning decision m3).

source.text: כֶּ֣סֶף מְרֻקָּ֞ע מִתַּרְשִׁ֣ישׁ יוּבָ֗א וְזָהָב֙ מֵֽאוּפָ֔ז מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חָרָ֖שׁ וִידֵ֣י צוֹרֵ֑ף תְּכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ לְבוּשָׁ֔ם מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֲכָמִ֖ים כֻּלָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Silver beaten from Tarshish is brought, and gold from Uphaz, [the] work of a craftsman and of [the] hands of a smith; blue and purple [is] their clothing; [the] work of skilled [ones are] all of them.

en.L: Silver beaten thin is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, \q the work of a craftsman and of the hands of a smith; \q blue and purple [are] their clothing; \q the work of skilled [men are] all of them.
en.B: Silver hammered into sheets is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz; \q they are the work of a craftsman and the hands of a goldsmith. \q Their robes are blue and purple; \q every one of them is the work of experts.
en.R: Thin sheets of silver are brought from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz. \q Craftsmen and goldsmiths make them into idols. \q The idols are dressed in blue and purple cloth. \q Skilled workers make every one of them.

decisions.choice: Tarshish: a distant port in the far west, known for its silver
decisions.reason: Tarshish traded in silver, iron, tin and lead (Ezekiel 27:12). It lay far across the Mediterranean, perhaps in Spain. The materials of the idols are brought from the ends of the known world, at great cost.

decisions.choice: Uphaz: a place known for gold, otherwise unknown
decisions.reason: The name appears only here and in Daniel 10:5 ("fine gold of Uphaz"). Some ancient translations read Ophir, the well-known land of gold (1 Kings 9:28), whose name differs by little in Hebrew writing.

decisions.choice: blue and purple: costly dyed cloth, the colors of kings and of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: These dyes, made from sea snails, were very expensive. They were used for royal robes (Judges 8:26) and for the curtains of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:1). The idols are dressed like kings.

decisions.choice: skilled: the same word as "wise" in verse 7
decisions.reason: The word means "wise" and is used of skilled workers (Exodus 28:3; Isaiah 40:20). The wisdom of the nations (verse 7) turns out to be the skill of the craftsmen who make their gods.

decisions.choice: smith (Literal); goldsmith (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means one who refines and works metal. Literal says "smith"; Balanced and Readable say "goldsmith", since he works the gold of this verse. Verse 14 has the same word.

decisions.choice: make them into idols ... The idols are dressed
decisions.reason: Readable says what the silver and gold are made into and who is dressed, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ אֱמֶ֔ת הֽוּא־אֱלֹהִ֥ים חַיִּ֖ים וּמֶ֣לֶךְ עוֹלָ֑ם מִקִּצְפּוֹ֙ תִּרְעַ֣שׁ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹֽא־יָכִ֥לוּ גוֹיִ֖ם זַעְמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But Yahweh [is] God truth; he [is] God living and king of perpetuity. From his wrath shakes the earth, and not endure nations his indignation.

en.L: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] God [in] truth; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the living God and everlasting King. \q At {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath the earth quakes, \q and nations cannot endure {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} indignation.
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is God in truth; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the living God, the eternal King. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is angry, the earth quakes, \q and the nations cannot withstand {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fury.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is the one true God. \q He is the God who is alive, the King who rules forever. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is angry, the earth shakes. \q The nations cannot stand up to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger.

decisions.choice: God in truth: the true God, real and faithful
decisions.reason: "God of truth" means the God who is real and can be relied on. It answers verse 14, where the idol is called a "lie".

decisions.choice: the living God: God who lives and acts
decisions.reason: Against the idols, which have no breath (verse 14) and cannot move (verse 5), the LORD is alive and acts (23:36; Deuteronomy 5:26; 1 Samuel 17:26).

decisions.choice: everlasting King: king for all time
decisions.reason: The word means a long, unbounded time. God's rule has no end, unlike the kings of the nations (Psalm 10:16; 29:10).

decisions.choice: verse 10 as the Hebrew text has it
decisions.reason: This verse is also missing from the old Greek translation; see verse 6.

decisions.choice: the one true God ... the God who is alive
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "true" and "living" mean here (meaning decisions m1 and m2).

source.text: כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן לְה֔וֹם אֱלָ֣הַיָּ֔א דִּֽי־שְׁמַיָּ֥א וְאַרְקָ֖א לָ֣א עֲבַ֑דוּ יֵאבַ֧דוּ מֵֽאַרְעָ֛א וּמִן־תְּח֥וֹת שְׁמַיָּ֖א אֵֽלֶּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: As this you will say to them: the gods who the heavens and the earth not made will perish from the earth and from under the heavens these.

en.L: Thus you shall say to them: \q "The gods who did not make the heavens and the earth \q will perish from the earth and from under these heavens."
en.B: This is what you are to say to them: \q "The gods that did not make heaven and earth \q will perish from the earth and from beneath these heavens."
en.R: Tell the nations this: \q "These gods did not make the sky and the earth. \q So they will disappear from the earth and from under the sky."

decisions.choice: this verse is in Aramaic
alternatives: a later note added in Aramaic
decisions.reason: This is the only verse in Jeremiah written in Aramaic, the common language of the Assyrian, Babylonian and Persian empires (2 Kings 18:26), which the nations around the exiles spoke. It reads as a short answer given to God's people to say to the nations in their own tongue. Why it stands here in Aramaic is not certain: it may be meant for use in exile, or it may be a note copied into the text. The Hebrew returns in verse 12.

decisions.choice: did not make ... will perish: a play on words
decisions.reason: In Aramaic the verbs "made" and "will perish" sound alike. The verse also uses two different forms of the word for "earth". The gods that did not make the world will be unmade from it.

decisions.choice: will perish: a statement of what will happen
decisions.reason: The verb form can state what will happen or wish it ("may they perish"). It is read as a sure statement, matching "they will perish" in verse 15.

decisions.choice: these: going with "heavens"
decisions.reason: The last word, "these", most naturally goes with "heavens", the heavens that the speaker and the hearers see. It could also point back to the gods: "... from under the heavens, these [gods]".

decisions.choice: the words to be said in quotation marks
decisions.reason: The words the people are told to say are a quotation inside the oracle, so they take double quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the nations ... So
decisions.reason: Readable says that "them" are the nations who worship these gods, and adds "So" to show the link between not making the world and perishing from it.

source.text: עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ מֵכִ֥ין תֵּבֵ֖ל בְּחָכְמָת֑וֹ וּבִתְבוּנָת֖וֹ נָטָ֥ה שָׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: [He is the] maker of [the] earth by his power, establisher of [the] world by his wisdom, and by his understanding he stretched out [the] heavens.

en.L: [He is] the maker of the earth by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power, \q who established the world by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wisdom, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} understanding {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stretched out the heavens.
en.B: It is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who made the earth by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power, \q who set the world firm by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wisdom, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} understanding spread out the heavens.
en.R: God made the earth by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power. \q He set the world firmly in place by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wisdom. \q He used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} understanding to spread out the sky.

decisions.choice: maker ... establisher: the LORD described by what he did
decisions.reason: The Hebrew returns after the Aramaic verse and begins with words describing the LORD of verse 10. Against the gods who did not make the heavens and the earth (verse 11), he is the one who did.

decisions.choice: verses 12-16 are repeated in 51:15-19
decisions.reason: These five verses appear again almost word for word in the oracle against Babylon (51:15-19). The thought of God founding the world by wisdom and understanding is also in Proverbs 3:19 and Psalm 104:24; stretching out the heavens in Isaiah 40:22; 42:5.

decisions.choice: world: the inhabited earth
decisions.reason: The word names the dry land where people live, set firm by God (Psalm 93:1; 96:10).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, since a new sentence begins and the verse before it spoke of the false gods.

source.text: לְק֨וֹל תִּתּ֜וֹ הֲמ֥וֹן מַ֨יִם֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיַּעֲלֶ֥ה נְשִׂאִ֖ים מִקְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ בְּרָקִ֤ים לַמָּטָר֙ עָשָׂ֔ה וַיּ֥וֹצֵא ר֖וּחַ מֵאֹצְרֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: At [the] sound of his giving, a roar of waters in the heavens, and he makes go up clouds from [the] end of the earth; lightnings for the rain he makes, and he brings out wind from his storehouses.

en.L: At the sound of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} giving forth [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice], [there is] a roar of waters in the heavens, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes clouds rise from the end of the earth; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes lightning for the rain \q and brings out wind from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} storehouses.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raises the clouds from the far edges of the earth. \q He makes lightning flash with the rain \q and brings the wind out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} storehouses.
en.R: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} thunders, the waters in the sky roar. \q He makes clouds rise up from far away at the edge of the world. \q He sends lightning with the rain. \q He brings out the wind from the places where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps it.

decisions.choice: at the sound of his giving: when he gives his voice, that is, thunders
decisions.reason: To "give one's voice" is a Hebrew way of saying "to speak out", and of God it means thunder (Psalm 18:14; 46:7).

decisions.choice: a roar of waters in the heavens: the rain held above the sky
decisions.reason: The heavens are pictured as holding waters above them (Genesis 1:7; Psalm 148:4), which roar down in the storm when God speaks.

decisions.choice: the same words as Psalm 135:7
decisions.reason: From "he makes clouds rise" to the end, the verse matches Psalm 135:7, and the wording of that psalm is used here. The verb forms differ slightly but the sense is the same: God, not any idol, sends the clouds, the lightning and the wind.

decisions.choice: clouds: mists that rise
decisions.reason: The word means "things lifted up" and is used of clouds or mists that rise from the horizon before rain (Psalm 135:7; Proverbs 25:14).

decisions.choice: When he thunders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "giving his voice" means (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew picture and supplies the missing object.

source.text: נִבְעַ֤ר כָּל־אָדָם֙ מִדַּ֔עַת הֹבִ֥ישׁ כָּל־צוֹרֵ֖ף מִפָּ֑סֶל כִּ֛י שֶׁ֥קֶר נִסְכּ֖וֹ וְלֹא־ר֥וּחַ בָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Is stupid every man without knowledge; is put to shame every smith by [the] idol, for a lie [is] his cast image, and no breath [is] in them.

en.L: Every {{gender:human|man}} is stupid, without knowledge; \q every smith is put to shame by [his] idol, \q for his cast image [is] a lie, and [there is] no breath in them.
en.B: Everyone proves senseless and ignorant; \q every goldsmith is shamed by his idol, \q for the images he casts are a fraud, with no breath in them.
en.R: Everyone who makes idols is stupid and knows nothing. \q Every goldsmith will be ashamed of the idol he made. \q His metal statues are fakes, and there is no life in them.

decisions.choice: every human is stupid, without knowledge: people shown up as senseless
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 8 ("brutish"). Beside the wisdom and understanding of God who made the world (verse 12), every person who trusts in idols is shown to know nothing. The verse is about people in general, but its target is those who make and worship idols.

decisions.choice: put to shame by his idol: disgraced when it fails him
decisions.reason: The goldsmith's own work lets him down when it cannot help or answer, and he is shamed by it (Isaiah 42:17; 44:9-11).

decisions.choice: a lie: a fraud, a false thing
decisions.reason: The cast image is called "a lie" because it pretends to be a god and is not one. It is the opposite of the "true God" of verse 10.

decisions.choice: breath: the breath of life
decisions.reason: The word means breath, wind or spirit. The images have no life in them (51:17; Habakkuk 2:19; Psalm 135:17).

decisions.choice: Everyone who makes idols
alternatives: Every person is stupid and knows nothing
decisions.reason: Readable narrows "every person" to those who make idols, which is the point of the verse in its context (meaning decision m1). It is a stretch from the general words, which could also mean that every person is senseless beside God's wisdom.

decisions.choice: the images he casts ... with no breath in them (Balanced); His metal statues ... no life (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves from "his cast image" to "them"; Balanced and Readable use the plural throughout so the sentence reads smoothly. Readable says "life" for breath.

source.text: הֶ֣בֶל הֵ֔מָּה מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה תַּעְתֻּעִ֑ים בְּעֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֖ם יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Futility [are] they, a work of mockeries; at [the] time of their punishment they will perish.

en.L: They [are] futility, a work of mockery; \q at the time of their punishment they will perish.
en.B: They are empty breath, a work to be laughed at; \q when the time comes to punish them, they will perish.
en.R: Idols are worthless, something to laugh at. \q When God comes to punish them, they will be destroyed.

decisions.choice: futility: empty breath
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, but now the idols themselves are called "breath".

decisions.choice: a work of mockery: something deceptive and laughable
decisions.reason: The word appears only here and in 51:18. It comes from a root meaning to mock or to lead astray, and so can mean a work that is ridiculous or one that deceives.

decisions.choice: the time of their punishment: when God comes to deal with them
decisions.reason: The word means a visit to inspect and settle accounts. Here it is the day God calls the idols, and those who trust them, to account (8:12; 11:23).

decisions.choice: Idols ... God comes
decisions.reason: Readable names the idols and says who punishes, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

source.text: לֹֽא־כְאֵ֜לֶּה חֵ֣לֶק יַעֲקֹ֗ב כִּֽי־יוֹצֵ֤ר הַכֹּל֙ ה֔וּא וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל שֵׁ֖בֶט נַֽחֲלָת֑וֹ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not like these [is the] portion of Jacob, for [the] former of the all he [is], and Israel [is the] tribe of his inheritance; Yahweh of hosts [is] his name.

en.L: Not like these [is] the portion of Jacob, for the one who formed all things [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, \q and Israel [is] the tribe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: The God who is Jacob's portion is not like these, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who formed all things, \q and Israel is the tribe {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} holds as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: But the God who belongs to Jacob's people is not like these idols, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made everything there is. \q He chose Israel to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} very own people. \q His name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: the portion of Jacob: God himself is the share that belongs to his people
decisions.reason: A portion is a share of land or goods. As the LORD's portion is his people (Deuteronomy 32:9), so the LORD himself is the portion of his people, more than any land (Numbers 18:20; Psalm 16:5; 73:26; Lamentations 3:24). Jacob stands for the whole nation descended from him.

decisions.choice: the one who formed all things: the maker of everything
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a potter shaping clay (18:4-6) and of God forming the first man (Genesis 2:7). The idol is formed by a craftsman; the LORD formed everything, including Israel.

decisions.choice: the tribe of his inheritance: the people God holds as his own
decisions.reason: An inheritance is a family's lasting share of land. Israel is God's own possession, the people he has claimed for himself (Psalm 74:2; Isaiah 63:17).

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts: the LORD, commander of all the armies of heaven and earth
decisions.reason: See Isaiah 1:9. The name closes the poem by setting the LORD, who commands the powers of heaven, against the idols that cannot move.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Balanced and Readable say "Armies" for "hosts", a word few readers now use for an army.

decisions.choice: The God who is Jacob's portion (Balanced); the God who belongs to Jacob's people ... chose Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says that the portion is God; Readable explains the picture as the God who belongs to his people and who chose them as his own (meaning decisions m1 and m3).

source.text: אִסְפִּ֥י מֵאֶ֖רֶץ כִּנְעָתֵ֑ךְ יֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּמָּצֽוֹר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Gather up from [the] land your bundle, [you who] dwell in the siege.

en.L: Gather up your bundle from the land, \q [you] who dwell under siege.
en.B: Pick up your bundle to leave the land, \q you who live under siege.
en.R: Pack your things to leave the land, \q you people of Jerusalem who are surrounded by enemies.

decisions.choice: you: a woman addressed, the city of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The verbs are feminine singular. The city is spoken to as a woman, told to get ready for exile. A new section begins here, after the poem on idols.

decisions.choice: bundle: a pack of belongings
decisions.reason: The word appears only here. It is probably a small bundle of goods, all that a person can carry into exile (compare Ezekiel 12:3-4).

decisions.choice: dwell: the form read aloud (qere)
decisions.reason: The written consonants have an older spelling of the feminine form "you who dwell"; the scribes marked the usual form to be read. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: under siege: Jerusalem surrounded by the Babylonian army
decisions.reason: The siege of Jerusalem by Babylon ended in its fall and the exile of its people (39:1-2; 52:4-7).

decisions.choice: you people of Jerusalem who are surrounded by enemies
decisions.reason: Readable names the city and explains what a siege is (meaning decisions m1 and m4).

source.text: כִּֽי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י קוֹלֵ֛עַ אֶת־יוֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ בַּפַּ֣עַם הַזֹּ֑את וַהֲצֵר֥וֹתִי לָהֶ֖ם לְמַ֥עַן יִמְצָֽאוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh: look, I [am] slinging out the inhabitants of the land at the time this, and I will bring distress on them, so that they will find.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Look, I am slinging out the inhabitants of the land at this time, \q and I will bring distress on them, so that they may find [it].
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q This time I am about to sling out the people of the land; \q I will hem them in so that they feel it.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q This time I will throw the people out of this land as if I were using a sling. \q I will bring trouble on them so that they will feel it.

decisions.choice: slinging out: hurling far away, as a stone from a sling
decisions.reason: The verb is used for slinging stones (Judges 20:16). Abigail says that God will sling away the lives of David's enemies (1 Samuel 25:29). The people will be thrown out of their land into exile.

decisions.choice: at this time: this time, unlike before
decisions.reason: The phrase sets this judgment apart from earlier threats and dangers that passed: now it will happen (16:21).

decisions.choice: bring distress on them: press them hard, hem them in
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the root for a tight, narrow place and is used of a siege that hems a city in (Deuteronomy 28:52).

decisions.choice: so that they may find [it]: so that they feel it fully
alternatives: so that they may find me
so that they will be caught
decisions.reason: The last words are short and unclear: "so that they may find" with no object. They are read as "so that they will feel it", the full force of the distress. Others read "so that they may find [me]", that is, seek God at last, or "so that they will be found", caught by the enemy.

decisions.choice: so that they feel it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in meaning decision m4; Literal keeps the bare verb and supplies the object in brackets.

source.text: א֥וֹי לִי֙ עַל־שִׁבְרִ֔י נַחְלָ֖ה מַכָּתִ֑י וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי אַ֛ךְ זֶ֥ה חֳלִ֖י וְאֶשָּׂאֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe to me because of my fracture; severe [is] my wound. And I said, surely this [is] a sickness, and I will bear it.

en.L: Woe [is] me because of my injury! \q My wound is severe. \q But I said, "Surely this [is] a sickness, and I must bear it."
en.B: Woe is me because of my injury! \q My wound is severe. \q But I said, "This is truly a sickness, and I must bear it."
en.R: How terrible this is for me! I am badly hurt. \q My wound is very bad. \q But I told myself, "This is a sickness I must live with."

decisions.choice: the speaker: Jerusalem, the people, voiced by the prophet
decisions.reason: The "I" is the city and people of Judah, pictured in verse 20 as a mother whose tent is torn down and whose children are gone. The prophet gives her voice, sharing her grief (compare 4:19-21; 8:18-23). The change of speaker is not marked.

decisions.choice: my injury ... my wound is severe: the ruin of the nation
decisions.reason: The first word means a break or fracture, used of the people's ruin (6:14; 8:11, 21). The word for "severe" means sick, grievous, and is used of wounds that do not heal (14:17; 30:12).

decisions.choice: surely this is a sickness, and I must bear it: accepting suffering that cannot be avoided
alternatives: this is only a sickness, and I can bear it
decisions.reason: The words can be a resigned acceptance: this is my sickness and I have to carry it. They can also look back to an earlier hope that it was only a passing illness that could be borne. The first fits the cry of grief in the verse.

decisions.choice: Woe is me (Balanced); How terrible this is for me! (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Balanced keeps the cry "Woe is me" and Readable puts it in everyday words. Readable adds "I am badly hurt" for "because of my injury".

source.text: אָהֳלִ֣י שֻׁדָּ֔ד וְכָל־מֵיתָרַ֖י נִתָּ֑קוּ בָּנַ֤י יְצָאֻ֨נִי֙ וְאֵינָ֔ם אֵין־נֹטֶ֥ה עוֹד֙ אָהֳלִ֔י וּמֵקִ֖ים יְרִיעוֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: My tent is devastated, and all my cords are snapped; my children have gone out from me and they are not; there is no one stretching out again my tent and raising my curtains.

en.L: My tent is devastated, \q and all my cords are snapped; \q my {{gender:children|sons}} have gone out from me, and they are no more; \q there is no one to stretch out my tent again \q and to set up my curtains.
en.B: My tent is destroyed, \q and all its ropes are snapped. \q My {{gender:children|sons}} have gone from me and are no more; \q there is no one left to pitch my tent again \q or to hang up my curtains.
en.R: My tent has been torn down. \q All its ropes are broken. \q My {{gender:children|sons}} have left me. They are gone. \q There is no one to set up my tent again \q or to hang its curtains.

decisions.choice: my tent ... my cords ... my curtains: my home
decisions.reason: The land and city are pictured as a woman living in a tent, the old word for a home. Its destruction is the ruin of the whole country (4:20). The opposite picture, a tent stretched out wide, is used for restoration (Isaiah 54:2).

decisions.choice: they have gone out from me and they are not: taken away, dead or in exile
decisions.reason: To say "they are not" is to say that they are lost (31:15; Genesis 42:36). The children are the people of the land, killed or carried off.

decisions.choice: children: sons and daughters
decisions.reason: The word is "sons" but here means the city's people as her children.

decisions.choice: its ropes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "its ropes" for "my cords", the tent ropes, since the tent is what they belong to.

source.text: כִּ֤י נִבְעֲרוּ֙ הָֽרֹעִ֔ים וְאֶת־יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א דָרָ֑שׁוּ עַל־כֵּן֙ לֹ֣א הִשְׂכִּ֔ילוּ וְכָל־מַרְעִיתָ֖ם נָפֽוֹצָה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For are stupid the shepherds, and Yahweh not they have sought; therefore not they have prospered, and all their flock is scattered.

en.L: For the shepherds have become stupid, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they have not sought; \q therefore they have not prospered, \q and all their flock is scattered.
en.B: For the shepherds have turned senseless \q and have not sought {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q so they have had no success, \q and all their flock is scattered.
en.R: The leaders of the people have been foolish. \q They have not asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help. \q So they have failed, \q and all their people have been scattered like sheep.

decisions.choice: the shepherds: the kings and leaders of Judah
decisions.reason: Kings and rulers were called shepherds of their people (2:8; 23:1-4; Ezekiel 34). The flock is the people.

decisions.choice: stupid: senseless, the same verb as for the idol makers
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verses 8 and 14. Judah's leaders have become as senseless as the makers of idols.

decisions.choice: sought: asked of God, turned to him
decisions.reason: To seek the LORD is to ask him for guidance and to turn to him in worship and obedience (21:2; 29:13).

decisions.choice: prospered: acted wisely and so succeeded
decisions.reason: The verb means both to act with insight and to succeed. Because they did not seek God, they have neither acted wisely nor succeeded.

decisions.choice: The leaders of the people ... asked the LORD for help ... scattered like sheep
decisions.reason: Readable explains the shepherd picture (meaning decision m1) and what it means to seek the LORD (m3), and keeps a hint of the flock with "like sheep".

source.text: ק֤וֹל שְׁמוּעָה֙ הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֔ה וְרַ֥עַשׁ גָּד֖וֹל מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֑וֹן לָשׂ֞וּם אֶת־עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה שְׁמָמָ֖ה מְע֥וֹן תַּנִּֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] sound of a report! look, it is coming, and a great shaking from [the] land of [the] north, to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a lair of jackals.

en.L: The sound of a report! Look, it is coming, \q and a great shaking from the land of the north, \q to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a lair of jackals.
en.B: Listen! A report! Here it comes: \q a great rumbling from the land of the north, \q to turn the cities of Judah into a wasteland, a haunt of jackals.
en.R: Listen! News is coming! \q A great army is thundering in from the north. \q It will turn the towns of Judah into ruins where only jackals live.

decisions.choice: the sound of a report: listen, news!
decisions.reason: "Sound of ..." at the start of a cry is a call to listen (3:21; Isaiah 40:3). The report is news of the army on its way.

decisions.choice: a great shaking: the rumble of an army on the march
decisions.reason: The word means a quaking or roar, used of chariots and marching troops (47:3; Nahum 3:2).

decisions.choice: the land of the north: Babylon, whose armies came from the north
decisions.reason: Armies from Mesopotamia came into Judah by the northern road. Jeremiah's warnings of the enemy from the north (1:14; 4:6; 6:1, 22) were fulfilled by Babylon.

decisions.choice: a desolation, a lair of jackals: as in 9:10
decisions.reason: The same words describe the ruin of Jerusalem and Judah in 9:10. Ruined towns are left to wild animals (49:33; Isaiah 34:13).

decisions.choice: A great army is thundering in
decisions.reason: Readable says what the great shaking is (meaning decisions m2 and m3).

source.text: יָדַ֣עְתִּי יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א לָאָדָ֖ם דַּרְכּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־לְאִ֣ישׁ הֹלֵ֔ךְ וְהָכִ֖ין אֶֽת־צַעֲדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: I know, Yahweh, that not to man [is] his way; not to a man walking and to direct his step.

en.L: I know, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q that not to {{gender:a human being|man}} [belongs] {{gender:their|his}} way; \q not to {{gender:one|a man}} who walks [does it belong] to direct {{gender:their|his}} steps.
en.B: I know, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q that {{gender:a person's|a man's}} way is not in {{gender:their|his}} own hands; \q no one who walks can set the course of {{gender:their|his}} own steps.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I know that people are not in control of their own lives. \q They cannot decide where their steps will lead.

decisions.choice: the speaker prays to God
decisions.reason: The voice of verses 19-20 now turns to God in prayer. Verses 23-25 are a prayer for the people, spoken as by the prophet on their behalf.

decisions.choice: a person's way is not their own: the course of a life is not in human control
decisions.reason: "Way" is the course of a life, and "steps" the path taken. Humans cannot steer their own lives; God directs them (Proverbs 16:9; 20:24). The prayer admits this, and so asks for God's correction rather than his anger (verse 24).

decisions.choice: man: any human being
decisions.reason: The two words mean a human being and a person; the saying is about everyone, men and women.

decisions.choice: gender spans
decisions.reason: Since the saying is about anyone (meaning decision m3), the inclusive wording is the default and "man" the alternative. Readable uses "people", which needs no alternative.

source.text: יַסְּרֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה אַךְ־בְּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט אַל־בְּאַפְּךָ֖ פֶּן־תַּמְעִטֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Correct me, Yahweh, only in justice, not in your anger, lest you make me few.

en.L: Correct me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, but with justice; \q not in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger, lest {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me few.
en.B: Correct me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, but in just measure, \q not in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger, or {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will bring me to nothing.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, correct me, but be fair. \q Do not punish me in anger, or there will be nothing left of me.

decisions.choice: correct: discipline, as a father his child
decisions.reason: The verb means to train by correction and punishment (2:19; 31:18; Proverbs 3:11-12). The prayer accepts discipline but asks that it not destroy.

decisions.choice: with justice: in fair measure
decisions.reason: "Justice" here is right measure, a limit set by what is fair. God later promises to correct his people "with justice" and not wipe them out (30:11; 46:28).

decisions.choice: me: the people speaking as one
decisions.reason: The "me" is the nation, as in verses 19-20, spoken for by the prophet.

decisions.choice: not in your anger: as in Psalm 6:2 and 38:2
decisions.reason: The psalms of lament ask in the same words that God not correct in his anger.

decisions.choice: make me few: reduce me to almost nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to make small or few. Under God's full anger the nation would be cut down until little or nothing was left (Ezekiel 29:15).

decisions.choice: in just measure ... bring me to nothing (Balanced); be fair ... nothing left of me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of meaning decisions m2 and m5 in plain words.

source.text: שְׁפֹ֣ךְ חֲמָתְךָ֗ עַל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יְדָע֔וּךָ וְעַל֙ מִשְׁפָּח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּשִׁמְךָ֖ לֹ֣א קָרָ֑אוּ כִּֽי־אָכְל֣וּ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַאֲכָלֻ֨הוּ֙ וַיְכַלֻּ֔הוּ וְאֶת־נָוֵ֖הוּ הֵשַֽׁמּוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Pour out your wrath on the nations that not know you, and on clans that on your name not call; for they have devoured Jacob, and devoured him and consumed him, and his pasture they have laid waste.

en.L: Pour out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath on the nations that do not know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q and on [the] clans \q that do not call on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; \q for they have devoured Jacob; they have devoured him and consumed him, \q and his pasture they have laid waste.
en.B: Pour out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury on the nations that have not known {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q on the peoples \q that never call on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. \q For they have swallowed up Jacob, swallowed him and finished him off, \q and left his homeland desolate.
en.R: Pour out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger on the nations that do not know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Pour it out on the peoples that do not worship {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q They have destroyed Jacob's people; they have swallowed them up and finished them off. \q They have ruined the land where they lived.

decisions.choice: the words of Psalm 79:6-7
decisions.reason: The verse is almost the same as Psalm 79:6-7, and that psalm's wording is used here. The differences: Jeremiah has "clans" where the psalm has "kingdoms"; Jeremiah's "for they have devoured" is plural where the psalm's is singular; and Jeremiah adds "they have devoured him and consumed him".

decisions.choice: clans: the families and peoples of the earth
decisions.reason: The word means a clan or extended family and is used for the peoples of the world (Genesis 12:3; Amos 3:2).

decisions.choice: know you ... call on your name: acknowledge and worship God
decisions.reason: To know God is to acknowledge him and belong to him, not just to know about him; to call on his name is to pray to him and worship him (Psalm 79:6; Genesis 12:8).

decisions.choice: pour out your wrath on the nations
decisions.reason: Having asked to be corrected with justice and not in anger (verse 24), the prayer asks that God's anger fall instead on the nations that destroy his people, who do not know him at all.

decisions.choice: Jacob ... his pasture: the people of Israel and their land
decisions.reason: Jacob stands for the nation descended from him. The word for "pasture" is the place where a flock settles, and so a home; the people are God's flock (verse 21).

decisions.choice: peoples
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "peoples" for "clans", since the word here means whole peoples, not small family groups (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: worship you; Jacob's people; the land where they lived
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 79:6-7, Readable says what calling on God's name means and who Jacob stands for (meaning decisions m3 and m5).
